name: Cabotegravir
route_note: gluteal IM injection monthly or every 2 months (treatment, with rilpivirine) or every 2 months (PrEP); optional oral lead-in tablets

discovery.note: Dolutegravir analogue whose low aqueous solubility and long half-life suit a nanosuspension depot injection.

tagline: Long-acting integrase inhibitor: HIV treatment or prevention injected every two months
summary: Cabotegravir is an integrase strand transfer inhibitor formulated as a long-acting intramuscular injection. Given every two months it is used alone for HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis, where it outperformed daily oral tenofovir/emtricitabine, and with rilpivirine as a complete long-acting HIV treatment. Oral tablets can be used as a lead-in or bridge.
mechanism: Like other INSTIs, cabotegravir binds the HIV integrase–viral DNA complex and blocks strand transfer, preventing integration of viral DNA into host chromosomes.

The injectable form is a nanosuspension that dissolves slowly from the gluteal muscle, giving a half-life of weeks. Low drug levels can persist for a year or more after the last injection (the 'tail'), which raises the risk of resistance if HIV is acquired during that time.
uses: HIV-1 pre-exposure prophylaxis in adults and adolescents weighing at least 35 kg (Apretude)
HIV-1 maintenance treatment with rilpivirine in virologically suppressed patients (Cabenuva, Vocabria + Rekambys)

history.title: HPTN 083 and 084
history.detail: Both PrEP trials are stopped early after injectable cabotegravir proves superior to daily oral TDF/FTC in men and transgender women (083) and in African women (084).

history.title: First approval
history.detail: Health Canada approves cabotegravir/rilpivirine for HIV treatment in March 2020; the EU follows in December.

history.title: Cabenuva and Apretude
history.detail: The FDA approves monthly Cabenuva in January and Apretude, the first long-acting injectable PrEP, in December 2021.

history.title: WHO guidance
history.detail: WHO recommends long-acting cabotegravir as an additional PrEP option and the Medicines Patent Pool signs a licence for generic production.

history.title: EU PrEP approval
history.detail: The EU approves Apretude for PrEP in September 2023.

pk.half_life: oral about 41 h; IM apparent half-life about 5.6–11.5 weeks
pk.bioavailability: oral not established; IM depot releases slowly

serious: development of INSTI resistance if HIV is acquired while on or after PrEP
safety.boxed_warning: Apretude: risk of drug resistance if used for PrEP in undiagnosed HIV-1 infection; test negative before each injection (US label).

facts: In HPTN 084, injectable cabotegravir reduced HIV incidence by about 89% compared with oral PrEP among women in sub-Saharan Africa.
It was the first long-acting injectable approved for HIV prevention.

references.title: Landovitz RJ et al. Cabotegravir for HIV prevention in cisgender men and transgender women (HPTN 083). NEJM 2021
